subject.title: fix(core): harden CLI lifecycle and suite isolation

question: Should Crabline intentionally reject existing strict manifests with retry counts above 10, or preserve the current accepted contract while introducing the guardrail compatibly?
rationale: The correct retry ceiling and upgrade behavior are compatibility-policy choices rather than mechanical bug fixes, and the PR does not establish an existing documented upper-bound contract.

options.title: Preserve Compatibility
options.body: Keep existing retry counts parseable, add a warning or opt-in strict bound, and cover upgrade behavior before enforcing a future hard limit.

options.title: Accept Breaking Validation
options.body: Keep the hard limit, but document the breaking contract and provide upgrade proof plus actionable operator guidance.

recommendation.title: Preserve Compatibility
recommendation.body: Keep existing retry counts parseable, add a warning or opt-in strict bound, and cover upgrade behavior before enforcing a future hard limit.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent work near the provider and channel architecture makes this the strongest available routing candidate for the manifest compatibility decision.
